question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(2x)^{x}.$ Its derivative is given by 

$$
{y}^{′}=(2x)^{x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(2x)^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((2x)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x))+(x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+x\cdot (\frac{1}{2x}\cdot 2) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=y=(2x)^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(2x)^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1.$
